title: Adapting Shared Responsibility Principles Framework to Authorised-transfer Scams
what_it_is: Adapting Shared Responsibility Principles Framework to Authorised-transfer Scams

sections.label: Government efforts against investment scams
sections.summary: The Government has stepped up measures against scams involving self-effected transfers, including investment scams, through messaging platform requirements, bank cooling periods and public education.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, scams are still a concern and as noted by the Member, investment scams recorded the highest losses among all scam types.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Government has stepped up efforts to combat scams involving self-effected transfers, including investment scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: For example, online messaging platforms will be required to implement measures that make it more difficult for unknown contacts to engage users without the end-users' consent, and to display warnings alerting users to the potential scam risks posed by such contacts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Major retail banks have progressively implemented cooling periods for higher-risk activities, such as adding of payees, raising of transaction limits and making large transfers that result in draining of accounts, to give consumers an opportunity to re-consider whether the transfer they intend to make is legitimate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: The Government will also continue to drive public education efforts to help the public better protect themselves against investment scams and make more informed financial decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: It is not suitable for scams involving self-effected transfers.

sections.label: MHA Bill against scams
sections.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs Bill passed yesterday deals with countermeasures against scams and would strengthen deterrence against scammers and enhance consumer protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: The Bill that was passed yesterday, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) Bill that deals with countermeasures against scams would also help, I think, to strengthen the deterrence against scammers and also to enhance the protection for consumers.

sections.label: Financial institutions' goodwill payments
sections.summary: Financial institutions and their staff work to reduce scam risk and make discretionary goodwill payments case-by-case, outside the SRF, based on victims' financial situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I think it is important to recognise this: that the FIs and the staff working in the FIs are trying their best to work together with us to try and reduce the risk of scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: I must also add that the FIs have also leaned forward to try and help on a discretionary basis to provide goodwill payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That means this is not part of the SRF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is what they do on their own – goodwill payment – on a case-by-case basis, based on the financial situation of the victims, especially those who come from more vulnerable backgrounds.
